title: Heating and cooling changes
keyIdea: Heating can melt a solid and boil a liquid; cooling can freeze a liquid; we measure the temperature in °C.

kid: Heat chocolate and it melts. Put water in the freezer and it turns to ice.
A thermometer tells us how hot or cold something is, in degrees (°C).
adult: Each material changes state at its own temperature. Water melts at 0 °C and boils at 100 °C. Chocolate melts at about 34 °C, which is why it melts in a warm hand.
Heating moves along solid → liquid → gas; cooling goes back. Reading a thermometer at the moment of change is a good first science measurement.

familyTip: Put a square of chocolate in your hand and one on a cold plate. Which melts first? Why?

practice.hint: Think about what happens to an ice cube held in warm hands.
practice.explain: Heating gives the ice energy, so it melts and turns into liquid water.

practice.hint: Think of the temperature inside a freezer, where ice cubes form.
practice.explain: Water freezes and turns into ice at 0 °C.

practice.prompt: Water is at {t} °C. How many degrees warmer until it boils at 100 °C?
practice.hint: Water boils at 100 °C. Take {t} away from 100 to find the gap.
practice.explain: 100 − {t} = {=100-t}, so the water needs to get {=100-t} degrees warmer.

practice.prompt: Room is {t} °C. Chocolate melts at 34 °C. How many degrees warmer?
practice.hint: Find the gap between the room temperature and 34 °C by taking away.
practice.explain: 34 − {t} = {=34-t}, so it needs to be {=34-t} degrees warmer for the chocolate to melt.

pool.hint: Think of a kettle bubbling when the water is as hot as it gets.
pool.explain: Water boils and turns into steam at 100 °C.

pool.prompt: Cooling a liquid can make it…
pool.hint: Think of what happens to water when you put it in the freezer.
pool.explain: Cooling a liquid enough makes it freeze and turn solid, like water turning into ice.

pool.prompt: A drink is {t} °C. It cools by {d} °C. What is it now?
pool.hint: Cooling makes the temperature go down, so take {d} away from {t}.

pool.prompt: Ice is at −{d} °C. How many degrees warmer until it melts at 0 °C?
pool.hint: Count up from −{d} to zero, one degree at a time.
pool.explain: From −{d} °C up to 0 °C is {d} degrees, so it needs to warm by {d} degrees.

pool.prompt: Why does chocolate melt in your hand?
choices: Your hand is warmer than its melting point
pool.hint: Chocolate melts at about 34 °C. Is your hand warmer or cooler than that?
pool.explain: Your hand is warmer than 34 °C, so it heats the chocolate past its melting point.

pool.hint: It is the tool that shows how hot or cold something is in °C.
pool.explain: We measure temperature with a thermometer.

pool.hint: Think of the cloud that comes out of a kettle when the water boils.
pool.explain: Heating water to 100 °C makes it boil and turn into steam, which is a gas.

visual.caption: Chocolate: drag the temperature. Watch it melt near 34 °C.

lab.caption: Heat the gas: the particles speed up. Cool it: they slow down.
